about.title: Hemet Slip & Fall and Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Hemet's commercial life runs along Florida Avenue, with State Street, Stetson Avenue, and Sanderson Avenue feeding shoppers into grocery stores, pharmacies, medical offices, and strip-mall parking lots. Those are the places where a wet entryway, a cracked curb, or a loose stair rail turns an ordinary errand into an emergency room visit. In California, a property owner is not automatically responsible just because you fell. You generally have to show the owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and did nothing to fix it or warn you. That notice question is where most Hemet premises cases turn, and it is why the first days matter so much. Photograph the spot before it is mopped or patched, get names of anyone who saw you fall, and ask in writing that surveillance footage be preserved before it is overwritten. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Riverside County residents with an independent attorney who handles premises claims on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Hemet Residents Use LawProactive After a Fall

items.title: Attorneys Who Understand the Notice Rule
items.desc: California requires proof that the owner knew or should have known about the hazard. The attorneys in our network know how to look for inspection logs, prior complaints, and maintenance records that speak to that question.

items.title: Fast Action on Evidence
items.desc: Store video is often erased within days or weeks. An attorney can send a preservation demand quickly and help you document the hazard before it disappears.

items.title: Honest About Comparative Fault
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, being partly at fault reduces a claim but does not erase it. Your attorney can explain how that applies to your situation without exaggerating or minimizing.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Hemet?
items.answer: For most private property falls in California, the deadline is two years from the date of the injury. If the fall happened on property owned by a public entity, such as a city sidewalk or a county building, a government claim generally must be filed much sooner, often within six months. Because of that difference, it is worth speaking with an attorney early rather than waiting.

items.question: I fell at a shopping center on Florida Avenue. Who is actually responsible?
items.answer: It depends on who controlled the area where you fell. A store tenant may be responsible for its own floor and entryway, while the property owner or management company may be responsible for the parking lot, walkways, and common areas. An attorney can review the lease and maintenance arrangements to identify the right party, and multiple parties are sometimes involved.

items.question: What if I was looking at my phone when I fell?
items.answer: California uses pure comparative fault, so distraction on your part can reduce what you recover but does not automatically bar your claim. The question is still whether the owner knew or should have known about the hazard and failed to address it. Be honest with your attorney about the circumstances so they can evaluate the claim realistically.
